instruction: Add a local small-language-model frontend strictly subordinated to the existing MPLPB authority rules. Present these five options, then implement Option 5 in full: Constrained Local Narrator. Configuration via MPLPB_NARRATOR_BACKEND=ollama|llamacpp|openai, MPLPB_NARRATOR_MODEL and MPLPB_NARRATOR_BASE_URL. Every generation runs strict answering first, supplies exact eligible spans and authority rules, validates output deterministically, and falls back on failure. Expose narrate(question, corpus_path, profile) and mplpb-combined narrate; keep models optional with --no-model. Do not change ownership rules, hash checks or finite grammar. Begin by scaffolding Option 5 as described above.
scope: Implement optional local narrator and CLI using existing strict answer coordinator and bounded loopback transport; Ollama, llama.cpp server and generic OpenAI-compatible server protocols.

Accept only complete unchanged ledger text in approved layouts; exact quotes alone and model confidence never establish support. Refusal/conflict/partial bypass inference; fresh strict proof and source/policy recheck after model attempt.
Add18 narrator tests and backend HTTP fixtures; document configuration, labels, exact citations, failure behavior and limits; preserve historical evidence.
validation: Baseline17 native tests passed with local sockets enabled; initial sandbox failed7 HTTP setups because sockets were denied. Logs retained.

First new tests had2 fixture errors: agreeing exact-field values were not a conflict in the existing coordinator. Corrected fixtures and added a separate multiple-owner statement control; no core rules changed.
Focused66 narrator/native/documentary tests passed5.406s exit0. Full archive regressions pending.
limitations: Live neural generation and independent semantic review NOT RUN; authored protocol fixtures are not model-quality validation.
Only complete exact answer formatting is allowed; arbitrary paraphrase, semantic extension, streaming and model-only claims are disabled.
Loopback cannot attest that a service never forwards remotely; local operators must disable forwarding. Socket timeouts do not establish total wall-time against malicious trickle responses.
